GUIDE: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the newly reopened Harlow Town Museum. I'm Fiona, and before you explore, I'll give you a quick overview. As some of you know, the museum was closed for eighteen months while the building was repaired. The roof had been leaking for years, and that was the main reason for the closure, although we've also taken the opportunity to redesign several galleries.
On the ground floor, you'll find the new Local Industries gallery. This town was famous for making rope, and there's a working machine that you can try. Please wait for a member of staff before you touch it, though. Next to it is the café, which now has twice as many seats as before.
On the first floor is the Costume gallery. Many visitors ask whether they can take photographs there. You can, but not with a flash, because strong light damages old fabric. The old map room, which used to be on that floor, has moved to the library across the road, so if you're interested in maps, you'll need to go there.
The second floor is new. It's the Discovery Zone, designed for children under twelve, with games and dressing-up clothes. Adults are welcome too, but only if they're with a child.
Now, a few practical things. Entry to the museum is still free, but there's a charge of £4 for the special exhibition on Victorian toys, which runs until the end of September. Bags larger than a small rucksack must be left in the lockers next to the main entrance. You'll need a one-pound coin, which you get back.
Finally, we're always looking for volunteers to help with tours and events. If that interests you, please pick up a leaflet at the information desk on your way out. Enjoy your visit.
question: What was the main reason the museum closed?
choices: The café was being made larger.
explanation: 屋根の 雨もりが the main reason と 言っている。ギャラリーの 再設計は ついでに した こと。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 museum reopening facilities

SPEAKER: Hello, and thanks for coming along to the Westbrook Community Garden open day. My name's Raj, and I'm one of the founders. The garden started six years ago on what was an empty car park. At first there were just five of us, digging on Saturday mornings. Now we have more than eighty members, and the garden produces vegetables, fruit and herbs all year round.
Let me explain how things work. Members pay twenty pounds a year. For that, you can come in whenever the gates are open, which is from seven in the morning until dusk. You don't get your own plot. Instead, everyone shares the work and everyone shares the harvest. We tried individual plots in the first year, but some were left empty for months, so we changed the system.
Each member is asked to give at least two hours a month. It doesn't have to be gardening. Some people help with our website, others bake for our monthly market stall.
Today's activities. At eleven, there's a talk on composting in the shed by the pond. At twelve, our youngest volunteers are running a seed-planting session for children, by the greenhouse. And all afternoon there's a plant sale near the main gate. All the money from that goes towards a new rainwater tank. Last summer was so dry that we spent a fortune on tap water.
One last thing: please don't pick anything today, however tempting the strawberries look! They're for our members' families this week. If you'd like to taste what we grow, the soup in the café tent is made entirely from our vegetables. It's free, but donations are welcome.
question: What was the site before it became a garden?
explanation: on what was an empty car park と 言っている。market は 今の 売店の 話で ひっかけ。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 community-garden open-day

PRESENTER: And now, as promised, some details about this year's Kelso Bay Food and Music Festival, which takes place over the bank holiday weekend. After last year's problems with traffic, the organisers have made some big changes. The most important is that the festival has moved from the seafront to Fairfield Park, which is larger and much easier to reach by public transport.
There'll be a free shuttle bus running every fifteen minutes from the train station. If you're driving, you'll need to book a parking space online in advance. There'll be no parking available on the day itself, and the organisers have asked me to stress that.
Tickets are £12 for a single day or £20 for the whole weekend, and children under fourteen go free. You can buy them online or at the tourist information centre, but not at the park gates. Again, that's to avoid the long queues we saw last year.
As for the programme, Saturday focuses on local bands, and the headline act is a jazz group called the Salt Street Five. On Sunday, the music is mainly folk, and there's a cookery stage where well-known local chefs will demonstrate dishes using seafood caught in the bay.
For families, there's a craft tent where children can make kites, and on Sunday afternoon there'll be a kite-flying competition. The prize is a family weekend at a holiday park.
The organisers are trying to make this the greenest festival yet. There'll be no plastic cups. Instead you pay a one-pound deposit for a reusable cup, which you get back when you return it. And finally, dogs are welcome, but they must be kept on a lead at all times.
question: Why has the festival changed location?
choices: because the seafront is being repaired
to make it easier to get to
answer: to make it easier to get to
explanation: larger and much easier to reach by public transport と 言っている。去年の 交通問題が 背景。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 radio local-festival announcement

LIBRARIAN: Good evening, and welcome to this information session about the newly refurbished Clayton Central Library. I'm Anne Marsh, the library manager.
I'd like to start with the most popular change: our opening hours. We used to close at six every evening. Now we stay open until eight on weekdays, which was the thing people asked for most in our survey. Weekend hours stay the same.
Next, the layout. When you come in through the main doors, the children's library is now on your left, where the newspapers used to be. We moved it so that families don't have to walk through the quiet study area. The newspapers and magazines are now on the first floor, next to the computers.
Speaking of computers, there are now thirty instead of twelve, and you can book them online. There's no charge for the first two hours each day, after which it's fifty pence an hour. Printing is ten pence a page for black and white.
We've also created a new room on the second floor called the Makerspace. It has a 3D printer, sewing machines and equipment for recording podcasts. To use it, you must first attend a short safety session, which runs every Saturday morning at ten.
A few people have asked about the café. Unfortunately, the company that ran it decided not to continue, so we're looking for a new operator. Until then, there's a water fountain on each floor, and you're welcome to bring your own snacks, as long as they're not hot food.
Finally, borrowing. You can now borrow fifteen items instead of ten, and the self-service machines also accept returns, so you won't need to queue at the desk. Any questions so far?
question: Which change did library users request most?
explanation: the thing people asked for most in our survey は 平日 8 時までの 開館。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 library refurbishment services

LIBRARIAN: Good evening, and welcome to this information session about the newly refurbished Clayton Central Library. I'm Anne Marsh, the library manager.
I'd like to start with the most popular change: our opening hours. We used to close at six every evening. Now we stay open until eight on weekdays, which was the thing people asked for most in our survey. Weekend hours stay the same.
Next, the layout. When you come in through the main doors, the children's library is now on your left, where the newspapers used to be. We moved it so that families don't have to walk through the quiet study area. The newspapers and magazines are now on the first floor, next to the computers.
Speaking of computers, there are now thirty instead of twelve, and you can book them online. There's no charge for the first two hours each day, after which it's fifty pence an hour. Printing is ten pence a page for black and white.
We've also created a new room on the second floor called the Makerspace. It has a 3D printer, sewing machines and equipment for recording podcasts. To use it, you must first attend a short safety session, which runs every Saturday morning at ten.
A few people have asked about the café. Unfortunately, the company that ran it decided not to continue, so we're looking for a new operator. Until then, there's a water fountain on each floor, and you're welcome to bring your own snacks, as long as they're not hot food.
Finally, borrowing. You can now borrow fifteen items instead of ten, and the self-service machines also accept returns, so you won't need to queue at the desk. Any questions so far?

explanation: you must first attend a short safety session と 言っている。オンライン予約は パソコンの 話。

RANGER: Welcome to the visitor centre at Glen Arran National Park. I'm one of the rangers, and I'll tell you about the walking routes before you head out.
Imagine the visitor centre is at the bottom of the map. Directly north of here, about a kilometre away, is Loch Brae, the lake. There's a flat path around it, which takes about an hour. It's suitable for wheelchairs and pushchairs, and it's the best place to see otters early in the morning.
To the east of the lake, there's a steep hill called Craig Dubh. The path to the top is rocky and quite challenging, so allow at least three hours there and back. The view from the summit is wonderful, but please note that the path is closed from April to June, because rare birds nest on the cliffs.
West of the visitor centre is the old pine forest. The forest trail is marked with yellow posts. It's about five kilometres long. Along the way you'll pass a waterfall, and next to it there's a picnic area with tables.
Now, a few safety points. Mobile phone signal is poor beyond the lake, so tell someone where you're going. The weather changes very quickly here, so even on a sunny day, take a waterproof jacket.
We also ask you to keep dogs on a lead, especially near the lake, because of the ground-nesting birds.
Finally, our guided walks. These leave from the front of the visitor centre at ten each morning and are free. On Wednesdays, the walk focuses on wild plants, and it's led by a botanist from the local university. Places are limited to fifteen, so please sign up at the desk.
question: Where is the lake in relation to the visitor centre?
explanation: Directly north of here ... is Loch Brae と 言っている。east は 丘、west は 森。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 national-park ranger-talk text-map

SPEAKER: Thank you all for coming to this public meeting about the redevelopment of Millbank Sports Centre. I'm Grace Adeyemi from the council's leisure department.
Let me begin with the timetable. Work will start in January and should be finished by the following October. The centre will close completely during that time. We did consider keeping part of it open, but the builders advised that it wouldn't be safe.
While the centre is closed, swimming lessons for schools will move to the pool at Riverside College, and the college has kindly agreed to let us use it at no cost. Other activities, such as yoga and badminton, will run in the community hall on Station Road.
So, what will the new centre include? The main pool will stay the same size, but we're adding a smaller learner pool, which will be heated to a higher temperature for babies and young children. The gym will double in size. And in response to many requests, there'll be an indoor climbing wall.
One thing we've had to drop is the sauna. It was in the original plans, but costs rose sharply last year and something had to go. I know that will disappoint some of you.
Regarding prices, membership fees will stay the same for the first year after reopening. After that, they'll be reviewed. Anyone over sixty-five, and anyone receiving unemployment support, will continue to get a fifty per cent discount.
The project is costing four point two million pounds. Most of that comes from a national sports grant, with the rest from the council's own budget.
We've set up a website where you can follow progress, including photos taken by a camera on the roof every day. Now, I'm happy to take questions.
question: During the building work, the sports centre will
explanation: The centre will close completely と 言っている。一部 開館も 考えたが 安全で ないと 判断。

SPEAKER: Hi everyone, and welcome to the Ashdown Farmers' Market. I'm Tess, the market manager. Since this is your first visit as a group, let me tell you how the market works and where to find things.
The market takes place on the first and third Saturday of every month, from eight until one. All our stallholders must grow, raise or make what they sell, and they must be based within forty miles of the town. That's the rule that makes us different from an ordinary market.
As you walk in from the car park, the first stalls you'll see are fruit and vegetables. Further along, under the clock tower, are the meat and fish sellers. If you want bread and cakes, the bakery stalls are in the covered area at the far end, which is useful if it's raining.
Some advice: arrive early if you want eggs or bread. They're usually sold out by about ten o'clock. On the other hand, if you come in the last half hour, many stallholders reduce their prices, especially for vegetables.
Most stalls now take cards, but a few of the smaller ones still only accept cash. There's a cash machine at the post office on the corner.
We also want to cut waste, so please bring your own bags. We no longer give out plastic ones. And if you bring back clean glass jars, the honey and jam sellers will refill them for a discount.
Every month we have a guest chef who cooks with ingredients from the market. Today it's someone from a restaurant in the town centre, and he's making a soup at eleven. You'll find him beside the fountain. Enjoy your morning.
question: What is special about the stallholders at this market?
choices: They are only there once a month.
explanation: grow, raise or make ... within forty miles と 言っている。月 2 回 開かれるので 3 番目は ひっかけ。
tags: IELTS Listening Part2 farmers-market guide

MANAGER: Morning, everyone, and welcome to your first day volunteering at the Hope Lane charity shop. I'm Pete, the shop manager. I'll run through the basics now, and you'll each spend some time with an experienced volunteer later.
First, timing. Please arrive ten minutes before your shift starts so you can put your things in the staff room. There's a locker for each of you. The code is on the notice board.
Most of you will start in the sorting room at the back, where we deal with donations. People leave bags at the back door, and we go through everything. Clothes need to be clean and in good condition. Anything torn or stained goes into the recycling sacks, not the bin, because a textile company buys them from us by weight.
Now, electrical items. We can't sell anything electrical unless it's been tested by a qualified electrician, and ours only comes in on Thursdays. So if you get a lamp or a kettle, put it on the shelf marked "awaiting test".
Books are one of our best sellers. Paperbacks are priced at one pound, and hardbacks at two, unless they're rare or collectable, in which case show them to me first.
When you're on the till, always ask customers if they're happy to sign the gift form. It allows the charity to claim extra money from the government on donated items. It doesn't cost the customer anything.
Breaks: you get fifteen minutes for every three hours. Tea and coffee are free in the staff room.
And one last thing — the most important rule. Never accept any donation for the shop while you're on the shop floor. Politely ask the person to take it round to the back door. Right, let's get started.
question: What happens to damaged clothes?
choices: They are sold to a textile company.
answer: They are sold to a textile company.
explanation: recycling sacks に 入れ、textile company が 重さで 買い取る。bin（ごみ箱）では ない。

MANAGER: Morning, everyone, and welcome to your first day volunteering at the Hope Lane charity shop. I'm Pete, the shop manager. I'll run through the basics now, and you'll each spend some time with an experienced volunteer later.
First, timing. Please arrive ten minutes before your shift starts so you can put your things in the staff room. There's a locker for each of you. The code is on the notice board.
Most of you will start in the sorting room at the back, where we deal with donations. People leave bags at the back door, and we go through everything. Clothes need to be clean and in good condition. Anything torn or stained goes into the recycling sacks, not the bin, because a textile company buys them from us by weight.
Now, electrical items. We can't sell anything electrical unless it's been tested by a qualified electrician, and ours only comes in on Thursdays. So if you get a lamp or a kettle, put it on the shelf marked "awaiting test".
Books are one of our best sellers. Paperbacks are priced at one pound, and hardbacks at two, unless they're rare or collectable, in which case show them to me first.
When you're on the till, always ask customers if they're happy to sign the gift form. It allows the charity to claim extra money from the government on donated items. It doesn't cost the customer anything.
Breaks: you get fifteen minutes for every three hours. Tea and coffee are free in the staff room.
And one last thing — the most important rule. Never accept any donation for the shop while you're on the shop floor. Politely ask the person to take it round to the back door. Right, let's get started.

explanation: ours only comes in on Thursdays と 言っている。
